text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.

- State-owned Postbanken bought 100 million crowns of preference shares in insurer Storebrand on Friday. The bank now holds three percent of votes in Storebrand, but it still will not comment on whether or not it will support the planned merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
- Former prime minister Gro Harlem Brundtland will most propably take over as head of the United Natios' World Health Organisation from Jult, 1998.
- Norway will continue to export tonnes of paper for recycling over the next few years after plans to build a new recycling plant in Norway were postponed.
- Technology shares on the Oslo Bourse are in free fall. Several high technology stocks fell by more than ten percent last month.

- Norwegian mortgage rates are largely dependent upon economic growth in Germany, says Audun Gleinsvik, chief economist at Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Norwegian politics are also important. A too relaxed fiscal policy could cause higher interest rates within a very short time.

- Dag Mejdell, the new CEO at Dyno Industrier, aims to sort out problems within management and the company's culture inherited from his predecessor. Mejdell warns against the lawsuits in the United States, which might be expensive for Dyno.
